questions.question: Which vector is the origin of $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: The vector whose coordinates are all one.
The vector whose coordinates are all zero.
Any vector with length one.
The vector with the largest coordinate equal to zero.

questions.question: How is the origin related to the zero vector in Euclidean coordinate space?
options: The origin is a scalar and the zero vector is not.
They are the same object.
The origin is any point on a line.
The zero vector is obtained by normalising the origin.

questions.question: What are the coordinates of the origin in $\mathbb{R}^3$?
Why are position vectors often drawn as arrows starting at the origin?
options: The origin changes depending on the vector.
It fixes the starting point for every position vector.
Every vector must end at the origin.
Only zero vectors can be drawn from the origin.

questions.question: What is special about the origin under vector addition?
options: Adding it changes every coordinate to one.
Adding it to a vector leaves the vector unchanged.
Adding it reverses the vector.
Adding it is undefined in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

questions.question: What is the origin in $\mathbb{R}^2$?
What is the distance from the origin to $(3,4)$ in the Euclidean plane?
Which vector starts at the origin and ends at the point $(-2,5)$?
If $v=(2,-1)$, what is $v+\boldsymbol{0}$?
Which point lies at the origin of $\mathbb{R}^4$?
What does it mean geometrically that the origin is the zero vector?
options: It is a vector of length one.
It is the reference point from which position vectors are measured.
It changes whenever a different position vector is measured.
It is the only point not belonging to $\mathbb{R}^n$.

questions.question: Is the origin always written with exactly two coordinates?
options: No; it has one zero coordinate for each dimension.
Yes; in $\mathbb{R}^n$ the origin is still written $(0,0)$.
No; it is the single number $0$ in every space.
No; it has one coordinate more than the space has dimensions.

questions.question: Why can equations involving the origin often be solved coordinate by coordinate?
options: Only the first coordinate must be zero.
The coordinates may sum to zero but be arbitrary otherwise.
Being equal to the origin means every coordinate is zero.
The origin has no coordinate description.

Which vector equation says that $x$ is the origin?
options: $x+\boldsymbol{0}=\boldsymbol{0}$ for all $x$
$x=\boldsymbol{0}$
$x\cdot x=1$

questions.question: Can a nonzero vector have some zero coordinates and still not be the origin?
options: No; one zero coordinate already makes it the origin.
Yes, because the origin has no coordinates.
Yes; all coordinates must be zero to be the origin.
No; nonzero vectors cannot contain zero coordinates.

questions.question: Why does the origin belong to every linear subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: Every subspace contains every point in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
The origin is chosen separately for each subspace.
A subspace must contain the zero vector.
Only affine lines contain the origin.

questions.question: For which $t$ does $(1,2)+t(3,-1)$ pass through the origin?
options: No real value of $t$.
$t=-\frac{1}{3}$, which only zeroes the first coordinate.
